Answers to the questions the dashboard's buttons ask, written in advance with an AI assistant (Claude) from the team's curated NASA documents and tests table, and checked against the cited source pages in a second AI pass; same format as the live chat's answers. answers.question: Why did test BASS:10 (PMMA, 21.9% O2) go out?

data.text: A 1 cm PMMA sphere burned in microgravity on the ISS at 21.89% O2 and 100.33 kPa and went out with the flow logged as 'fan off' (0 cm/s).
The BASS deck reports a PMMA sample of 15-mm initial diameter, at a nominal 17% O2, 101.3 kPa and under 1 cm/s, whose flame survived a nitrogen jet and went out at zero flow.
The same sphere's last run, BASS:11, at the same 21.89% O2 and 100.33 kPa (flow logged as 'at 42', no unit), burned until its fuel ran out and is labelled burned.

BAS-01 Appendix D reports that sample 19, a 1-cm PMMA sphere of initial mass 617.5 mg, was completely consumed in four tests; its Table D.2 gives test 20, this run by test number (the team's match), a burn of 1 min 15 s.

inferred.text: This flame went out at 21.89% O2, above the nominal 17% O2 at which the BASS deck shows PMMA spheres burning in flow; the logged fan turn-off, not the oxygen level, is what coincides with the extinction.

other_side.note: the same sphere's last run burned until its fuel ran out

lead.text: BASS:10 (1 cm PMMA sphere, 21.89% O2, microgravity) went out with the fan logged off; the sphere's last run burned until its fuel ran out (BASS:11).
